preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide [j] to a velar stop [ɡ]. The classic case is Holtzmann's law (Verschärfung) in North Germanic, where the Proto-Germanic geminate glide *-jj- hardened to -ggj- (Gothic -ddj-), as in *ajją > Old Norse egg 'egg' and *Frijjō > Proto-Norse *Friggju > Old Norse Frigg. West Germanic left the glide unhardened (Old High German ei, Friia).

examples.note: Holtzmann's law: geminate *-jj- hardened to a velar stop in North Germanic; cf. Crimean Gothic ada (-ddj- in East Germanic) and the unhardened Old High German ei, Old English ǣġ.
The same hardening of *-jj-; Old High German Friia keeps the glide.
